pages.title: CA Administration: Provisioners, Admins, Policies, ACME EAB
pages.purpose: Explain the admin-side command groups: step ca provisioner (add/list/remove/update, encrypted provisioner keys, webhook), step ca admin (x5c-based admin credentials via NewAdminClient, linkedca), step ca policy (authority/provisioner/acme policy context), step ca acme eab, and the hidden step api token group.
instructions: Explain the NewAdminClient fallback flow (prompt for admin subject, generate admin cert via a sign request) from utils/cautils/client.go.
Note which commands require a CA with remote management / database-backed provisioners where the source says so.

pages.title: Command Framework and Lifecycle
pages.purpose: Explain how a command is registered (init + command.Register), how the urfave/cli app is constructed (help templates, version, flag stringification, global --config), plugin dispatch for unknown top-level commands, and include a change guide for adding a new command.
instructions: Cover plugin.LookPath/Run semantics including Windows PATHEXT behavior from internal/plugin/plugin.go.
Trace the exact call path from main() to an action function, citing internal/cmd/root.go line evidence.

pages.title: Architecture Overview
pages.purpose: Explain the repository's overall structure: the cmd/step entrypoint, internal/cmd app bootstrap, the command registration model, top-level package ownership (command, utils, token, internal, flags, exec), and how the CLI relates to external libraries (smallstep/certificates, go.step.sm/crypto, cli-utils).
instructions: Base ownership-boundary statements on actual package imports and the blank-import registration list in internal/cmd/root.go.
Do not describe deployment or runtime hosting behavior that the repository does not establish.

pages.title: Build, Release, and Packaging
pages.purpose: Explain the build and release pipeline: Makefile build/version/ldflags logic, goreleaser configuration (builds, archives, nFPM, checksums/signing), platform packages (debian, docker, systemd, powershell), scripts, cosign.pub, and the GitHub Actions workflows for CI, release, and package publishing.
instructions: Describe package formats and targets from .goreleaser.yml and the packaging directories without inventing release cadence.
Document how VERSION is derived (GITHUB_REF, git describe, .VERSION) exactly as the Makefile implements it.

pages.title: Configuration, State Files, and Flags
pages.purpose: Explain the CLI's on-disk state under STEPPATH (defaults.json, contexts.json, profiles, ca.json, certs/root_ca.crt, tpm dir, plugins dir), the step path command, the global flags system in flags/flags.go (including ParseCaURL https-only rule, template data, KMS URI), environment variables, and the --config flag.
instructions: Document the ParseCaURL/ParseCaURLIfExists behavior differences and the IPv6 bracket handling.
State file locations relative to step.Path()/BasePath() as established by cli-utils usage in this repo; where the repo does not pin a default STEPPATH, say so.

pages.title: Crypto Toolkit Commands
pages.purpose: Explain the step crypto command family (jwt, jwk, jws, jwe, jose, key, hash, kdf, nacl, otp, rand, winpe, change-pass, keypair), the KMS-aware key loading in internal/cryptoutil, KDF implementations in internal/kdf, plus the auxiliary step base64 and step fileserver commands.
instructions: Explain cryptoutil.IsKMS filename-vs-KMS-URI disambiguation and the Attestor interface.
Keep this page at the subsystem level: flag surface per subcommand group, KMS URI handling, and output conventions, not an exhaustive flag dump.

pages.title: Failure Handling and Security Conventions
pages.purpose: Explain the cross-cutting error model (errs to ExitError, messenger interface output, STEPDEBUG, panic handler, exit codes), file permission conventions for written key/cert files, and the security gates: https-only CA URLs, root fingerprint validation, subtle/insecure flags, unsafe token parsing, and password handling.
instructions: Cite the exact exit-code behavior: run() returns 1, panicHandler exits 2, exec errorAndExit uses os.Exit(-1).
Do not claim guarantees (e.g., about key storage) beyond what the source comments and code establish.

pages.title: Bootstrap, Root Distribution, and Contexts
pages.purpose: Explain step ca bootstrap (fingerprint-validated root download, defaults.json, context creation, truststore install), team/authority bootstrap against api.smallstep.com, step ca root/roots/federation/health, and the context/profile/authority system (contexts.json, step.Contexts, UseContext).
instructions: Distinguish what the CLI writes (defaults.json, root_ca.crt, contexts.json) from what the server provides.
State the default team bootstrap endpoint and redirect URL exactly as in bootstrap.go.

pages.title: Certificate Issuance Flow (Token + Sign)
pages.purpose: Trace the end-to-end online issuance path: step ca token (provisioner discovery, per-provisioner token generation, audiences) and step ca certificate (CSR creation, SAN handling per token type, subject validation, CA sign, file writes), plus the ACME branches and offline branch points.
instructions: Document each provisioner type's token path (JWK, OIDC, X5C, Nebula, SSHPOP, K8sSA, GCP/AWS/Azure, ACME/SCEP errors) as implemented in token_flow.go and offline.go.
State explicitly where SANs come from per token type (certificate_flow.go CreateSignRequest) rather than assuming server behavior.

pages.title: Offline CA: step ca init and OfflineCA
pages.purpose: Explain step ca init (flag validation matrix, RA variants StepCAS/CloudCAS, KMS options, deployment types, generated PKI files and ca.json) and the OfflineCA wrapper (singleton, authority.New, audience derivation, Sign/Renew/Revoke/SSH method semantics including the TLS-transport mTLS trick).
instructions: Enumerate the init flag incompatibilities exactly as coded in initAction.
Explain why OfflineCA is a process singleton (badgerDB lock comment) and the consequences for mixed online/offline use in one invocation.

pages.title: Renewal, Revocation, and Rekey
pages.purpose: Explain step ca renew (mTLS vs token auth, expires-in jitter, daemon mode, pid/signal/exec hooks, offline mode), step ca revoke and rekey, the SSH equivalents (step ssh renew/rekey/revoke), and needs-renewal checks.
instructions: Cover the offline Renew/Revoke/Rekey wrappers in utils/cautils/offline.go that read the client cert from the http.Transport.
Document the daemon scheduling defaults (2/3 of time to expiration) only if they are stated in the source; otherwise state what the source establishes.

pages.title: OAuth 2.0 and OIDC Client
pages.purpose: Explain the step oauth command: provider discovery, loopback (default), manual, device, JWT bearer, and two-legged authorization flows, the local callback server, console mode, OIDC bare tokens, and how step oauth feeds OIDC provisioner tokens to CA commands.
instructions: Cover the local server port/listen flags and the implicit (deprecated) handler behavior as coded.
Describe each authorization mode's control flow as implemented in the Do* methods of command/oauth/cmd.go.

pages.title: SSH Certificates and Single Sign-On
pages.purpose: Explain the step ssh command group: certificate signing (user/host), login/logout via ssh-agent, step ssh config (templates, roots/federation inspection), proxycommand (host registry lookup, exec of ssh), check-host, hosts, and key operations, plus internal/sshutil helpers.
instructions: Document agent integration (SSH_AUTH_SOCK, add/remove) as implemented in internal/sshutil/agent.go.
Explain the proxycommand exec chain (exec.Exec/Run, signal forwarding) with evidence from exec/exec.go and command/ssh/proxycommand.go.

pages.title: Testing Strategy
pages.purpose: Explain how the repository is tested: colocated unit tests, the testscript/txtar integration suite in integration/ (TestMain maps step to cmd.Run), testdata conventions, and the make test/race/lint targets plus CI workflows.
instructions: Cover which linters/checks run via the Makefile (golangci-lint with shared config, govulncheck) and the short-mode test invocation.
Explain how testscript.Main registers the step command so tests run the real command tree.

pages.title: Quickstart
pages.purpose: Get developers building, testing, and running the step CLI: environment bootstrap, make targets, integration test entry points, and a first end-to-end certificate flow (offline init and online bootstrap paths).
instructions: Show the minimal offline flow (step ca init -> step ca certificate --offline) and the online flow (step ca bootstrap -> step ca token -> step ca certificate -> step ca renew) using flags that exist in the command definitions.
Verify every make target and command you document against the Makefile and docs/local-development.md; do not invent targets.
